reviews.text: In addition to the technological component, this film poses a fair criticism on the little capacity human beings have to conserve this beautiful planet... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gianmarco Farfán

reviews.text: With plenty of American Dream nostalgia and a great performance from Tom Hanks, AppleTV+’s Finch is ultimately a story about love in its purest form.
reviews.author: Serena Seghedoni

reviews.text: Finch is far from being the most impressive, imaginative post-apocalyptic, survival film, but it's still a captivating, character-driven story that boasts an emotionally resonant, meaningful personal journey.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Hanks proves once again why he has a tremendous eye for material, and why he is simply one of the best in the business.
reviews.author: Brian Rowe

reviews.text: There isn’t more to the story here. You can’t write a robot who has feelings, treat them poorly, use them, and pretend it’s a heartwarming experience. This is how we teach young people about “love, friendship, and the meaning of human life”?
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: There’s an effortless connectability Hanks has with his audiences and he make us feel a part of any story he’s helping to tell. In this case, it’s a story of the human experience. It’s a beautiful fable about what makes us who we are.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text:
Finch makes you believe that even in the darkest moments, there still remains something worth fighting and living for.
[Full review in spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Finch isn't the most original or exciting sci-fi movie you'll ever see, but it's a charming road trip adventure anchored by yet another incredible performance from Tom Hanks.
reviews.author: Scott Campbell

reviews.text: Finch has its problems, chiefly an overreliance on sentimentality and stretched movie logic. But with two fine storytellers at work, its sure to leave many in a blubbery mess.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: "'Finchs' relative softness makes 'A Quiet Place' look like 'The Road,' but after the year and a half weve just had theres something to appreciate about how it lets us down easy."
reviews.author: David Lynch

reviews.text: There is not just a charming personality to the film but a deeper more poignant foundation of humanity and fatherhood.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: A surprisingly tender film, Finch is the kind of hopeful science fiction that the world desperately needs.
reviews.author: Christopher Cross

reviews.text: At its core, Finch doesnt seem to know what it wants to be...Its a bit dark for kids, and a bit obvious for adults. It wants to be a parable but doesnt have enough to say. Ultimately, Finch would work better as a Pixar short.
reviews.author: Frederick Blichert

reviews.text: Finch simply doesn't have enough excitement to work as one-man show.
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: While not perfect, I would recommend Finch to anyone who wants to laugh and smile during a movie in this kind of tragic setting.
reviews.author: Shah Shahid

reviews.text: A post-apocalyptic road movie that, in my opinion, has noble intentions that are built slowly with good acting from Tom Hanks, but the lack of parts drags its narrative onto conventional paths. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Director Miguel Sapochnik and writers Craig Luck and Ivor Powell muse on the meaning of life with a photogenic dog, a kinda creepy robot named Jeff and the singular Tom Hanks.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: Only Tom Hanks can make me develop an interest in a dog and a robot. A tear duct activator due to its message of purpose and survival.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: Despite its conventional formula, Finch finds redemption in Tom Hanks' performance and its commendable visual effects. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: The trouble with this kind of mix-tape moviemaking is that when your film is dominated by echoes, it's difficult to make your own voice heard.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: Craig Luck and Ivor Powell's script doesn't toss many curveballs or proclaim something profound, relying on endearing plot development and its trio of stars to carry the show.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: We'll always love Tom Hanks, but his patented, aw-shucks everyman shtick is starting to grow a little threadbare.
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: Hanks' weary, weathered face, his eyes somehow sad and sparkling at the same time, sells the hell out of it.
reviews.author: Gena Radcliffe

reviews.text: Tom Hanks is at his best in another "solo" performance a la "Castaway".
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Despite the sweetness and affection demonstrated in the relationships, the film lacks twists and - just like the chatty robot - feels artificial.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Even if it doesn't always compute, it is a rewarding journey.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Overall, a worthy and endearing work to be casually liked, rather than totally loved.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Deserves to be treated as more than a pandemic castoff movie, a film that succeeds in fully transcending its premise
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: The big sell is the thoroughly convincing turn by Tom Hanks...It's his interaction with Jeff that truly humanizes the robot rather than the quality of the VFX, super though they are.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: We have Tom Hanks doing his thing, being the most likable guy ever, with a cool robot. It's a good small science fiction movie from everyone involved.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: Earth is in danger from climate change, and I would rather spend the time we have left rewatching old Hanks movies that are so much livelier and less portentous, like Sleepless in Seattle or Splash.
reviews.author: Hannah Brown

reviews.text: A moving, earnest tale of friendship and what it means to be human.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Nothing new but it's interesting that the other "humans" are always perceived as an imminent threat from which we must flee. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: [Finch] is content with an innocent tone and a certain eighties cinema spirit (note the producers are Robert Zemeckis and the Amblin company that Steven Spielberg founded), which is enjoyed but leaves one wanting more. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: It can be viewed with some appreciation, especially for Hanks' work. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: There's no excuse for a sci-fi/drama road trip movie to be this unaffecting and uninteresting.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: Simple but effective, the movie asks us to care not because of any big twist, or gigantic set piece, but for the sake of pure human empathy.
reviews.author: Aaron Dicer

reviews.text: Instead of an inanimate volleyball to keep [Hanks] company, he's got his newly minted 'bot...
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Hanks is phenomenal, because - outside of those Robert Langdon movies - it's the only gear he has. But it's not enough to elevate a script as generic and derivative as the one here.
reviews.author: Dustin Rowles

reviews.text: If that sounds like an unweildy mashup of unlikely bedfellows... well, it is. But Hanks is such a watchable presence that he makes this one-man show worthwhile.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: It's a nominal tearjerker playing on the emotions of the type of people who leave a lot of money when they die to their dogs and nothing to those ungrateful children.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: A charming little Sci-Fi flick that will make you smile and even make you shed some tears. Tom Hanks delivers as always. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: It is a man on a mission story and, though a little corny, has a lot of charm.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: As he proved in Cast Away, Tom Hanks solo can keep anyone's attention for hours. Paired with a rather good dog actor and some very good effects for Jeff, this is an easy watch.
reviews.author: Jonathan Roberts

reviews.text: Tom Hanks ten years after the end of the world in his usual bed of pain: alone... a genial blend of many things, not least Hanks' affinity for playing goodness and kindness and hope wherever his character may find themselves in their miserable existence.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: Hanks does what he can with this demeaning material, because he always gives his best, but what can you do with a movie where the dog gets all the good close-ups?
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: Stirring post-apocalyptic thrills and breezy humour into a warm and sentimental drama, director Miguel Sapochnik holds the interest in this gently rolling narrative.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Hanks is excellent (he always is) but even his prodigious talent can't salvage a robot coming-of-age story with not much new to say.
reviews.author: Chelsea Steiner

reviews.text: It moves at an absorbing pace driven by Hanks's performance, empathetic and sober, combined with Jones's loveable Jeff.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: For a film where just one of the three named characters is an actual person, Finch exists as a surprisingly moving exploration of what it means to be human.
reviews.author: Kimber Myers

reviews.text: Adequate but hardly exceptional, this schmaltzy post-apocalyptic road trip movie probably wouldn't have made much of a dent in theatres; on smaller screens it's a not-bad but quickly forgettable star vehicle.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Finch has its issues - it's got some narrative holes and the inconsistent tone doesn't always click. But it works far more than it doesn't...It's a simple story about a man, his dog and his robot. A simple story about the end of the world.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: Reminded me of the sci-fi short stories I read as a kid. Who would you rather spend your final days on Earth with other than Tom Hanks. Except maybe a robot created by Tom Hanks. And his dog. A sad, sweet movie.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: A totally charming -- and pretty moving -- riff on the American road movie that takes a refreshingly ambivalent view of a post-human future.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: A dystopian coming of age story with puppy dog eyes that willfully avoids all the surprise, suspense and danger expected in the genre and then defies you to reject it.
reviews.author: Mark Keizer

reviews.text: Director Miguel Sapochnik sustains the mood with care, delivering a serio-comic blend of sci-fi and road movie that's both sweet and soulful.
reviews.author: Kevin Harley

reviews.text: Hanks plus dog plus robot might feel too cute for its own good, but director Miguel Sapochnik, a frequent helmer of the massive battle episodes of Game of Thrones, finds joyful and mournful notes to play while still hitting all the familiar beats.
reviews.author: Dan Jackson

reviews.text: On the surface, Finch is a winsomely eccentric science-fiction adventure about a man, his dog, and his son, setting off on a quest for a better tomorrow...
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: ...there's plenty of charm to spare in this robotic Odd Couple...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Tom Hanks proves he's immensely watchable in a moving + heartfelt sci-fi drama that tugs my heartstrings. For a film with such a dire subject matter, it ends with an uplifting and hopeful note that leaves a sweet, instead of bitter, after taste.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: An unusual road movie full of life lessons for an engineer, a dog, and a robot.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: This is not the first time we've seen a toxic post-apocalyptical world, but the humanity displayed by Hanks is indeed unique and consummately moving.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: Finch is a sweet post-apocalyptic road movie about the unforeseeable friendships we forge in a world that is aggressively going to the dumpster.
reviews.author: Shikhar Verma

reviews.text: Bittersweet and tense sci-fi film, built around a post-apocalyptic concept.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: A quietly simple, elegant, gem of a sci-fi tale.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: Miguel Sapochnik skilfully steers his affecting family drama away from the pitfalls of sentimentality. Landry Jones is terrific as Robot Jeff, a synthetic made sympathetic, struggling to understand the contradictions of the man who made him.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: Everything suitably gets explained by the time the world ends. Or does it?
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Finch makes you laugh, tense up, and get a lump in your throat, all in just under two hours.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Finch is a marvel of man connecting with machines, lifted by an excellent Tom Hanks performance, surviving together at the end of the world.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: The efforts to tug on our heartstrings don't always work, but "Finch" is a sweet-natured comic drama about what it means to be human.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: The droid's annoying and the emotions are cloying in the post-apocalyptic Apple TV+ movie.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: This is the most amiable post-apocalyptic movie you're probably ever going to see.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: If you're a dog person and a Tom Hanks person, then this is really a no-brainer.
reviews.author: Andy Klein

reviews.text: Watching Hanks here is like Michael Jordan on the Wizards...something ain't right. Finch might be the most unoriginal movie this year.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Most sci-fi fans have been down this dystopian road many before -- and with better movies.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: It's thoughtful escapism, made richer by its amiably charismatic star.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: The charm that Tom Hanks brings and the humanity that Tom Hanks brings is what makes this movie work.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Knowing that Finch was at one time destined for the big screen only adds to the film's doleful aura, the presiding sense of a once glittering thing lost to the tumult and wear of time.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: The goal is clearly to evoke "Cast Away... But this one fails to worm its way into your heart, no matter how hard it tries, resorting to even the hoariest of tricks, a soundtrack fortified with beloved pop songs.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Well before the baffling final scenes, the movie has tied itself in knots.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: -It's a movie that kind of sneaks up on you with a touching ending if you're willing to lean in and give it a try. And you may even need a Kleenex.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: The movie has a whole "PG-rated Chappie" vibe that almost makes it heartwarming. The refusal to grapple with any ethical questions relating to Finch's actions, though, is a major letdown.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: There's a lot to like and admire about this post-nuclear family road movie, and, if you're a fan of Hanks, this is two hours definitely well spent.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Thankfully, director Miguel Sapochnik has Tom Hanks and a sweet rescue named Seamus and his decision to just embrace his material's corniness works in its favor. This movie is made for anyone who's ever noted that DOG is GOD spelled backwards.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Call it Wall E meets Castaway, call it the Amblin Entertainment version of Chappie, just don't call it not delightful.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: It feels very much at home on the small screen, however, possibly the mellowest post-apocalyptic story you'll ever see. And Hanks is perfectly cast.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: The film's tone finds a decent balance: it's often funny, though it's tempered by the dire circumstances of the world they're in, and it's often moving, though the humor keeps it from being saccharine.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: While this may seem like quite the downer, the casting of Hanks as Finch is the perfect spoonful of sugar to help the weighty medicine go down.
reviews.author: Burt Peterson

reviews.text: The relatively simple story - a man, a robot, and a dog go on a road trip after an apocalypse - turns out to have a surprising amount of layers and emotional depth.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: The movie seems like an odd combination of WALL-E and The Day After Tomorrow, and I mean that in the best way possible.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: Finch is a surprising subversion of the post-apocalyptic genre and a film that tugs on the heartstrings thanks to Tom Hanks and Caleb Landry Jones' performances.
reviews.author: Collier Jennings

reviews.text: Rarely has the devotion between human and canine felt as vital and affecting as in this bittersweet science-fiction vehicle for Tom Hanks, which is an adventure of discovery and rebirth inadvertently tailor-made for an age of lockdowns and quarantines.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: The sci-fi drama showcases a stringy solo Hanks as we may have never seen him before.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: A poignant, touching, rather poetic - and refreshingly low-key - road movie that really does encapsulate that hoary old SF cliché "what it means to be human".
reviews.author: Paul Mount

reviews.text: Hanks is fine, he almost always is, but this is a role that just allows him to coast on his reputation as America's Cinematic Dad.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: While "Finch" doesn't have the same emotional resonance as "Cast Away," it's surprising how Hanks makes us deeply care about his character's plight.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: The Hanks magic and optimism, the last days of the planet and the sweet dog and robot are all but overwhelming; it's hard to watch but also endlessly about love. Not as sappy as the trailer would have you believe.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: If there's one thing Finch makes clear, it's that if you're going to have company for the end of the world, you could do a lot worse than an android named Jeff.
reviews.author: Rick Marshall

reviews.text: The very idea is so tear-jerking on so many levels that a filmmaker runs the risk of turning off the audience by leaning too hard in any direction. That's where Hanks comes in.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: Hanks does his considerable best with Finch's revelations and confrontations, but the writing lets him down.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Although Finch dips a bit too much into sentimentality, watching Hanks operate in a role he has experience with makes the film worth a watch.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Ultimately, I couldn't help but find this flawed robot, and this flawed film, endearing.
reviews.author: Rain Jokinen

reviews.text: With another performer playing the part, it's possible this nearly two-hour offering could have easily gone sideways into camp or bad sci-fi, but Hanks grounds the material in easy to watch believability.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Tom Hanks, his dog and a robot charm in a post-apocalyptic road movie assembled with care and a light touch.
reviews.author: Matt Maytum

reviews.text: Hanks does his level best to keep the film from drifting into cuteness or sentimentality, focusing instead on the jeopardy, his underlying anxiety and things preying on his mind. It adds up to a movie with real heart, that is surprisingly touching.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: Tom Hanks, a cute dog and a lovable robot -- only the hardest of hearts could resist such a trio. This is movie gold.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: It's rare for post-apocalyptic stories to focus on unambiguously good people, but Hanks makes Finch easy to believe in.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: "Finch" is all concept, no movie, like something Pixar would have discarded in an early brainstorming session or what a Terminator would invent as a psy-ops campaign before the takeover.
reviews.author: Robert Abele

reviews.text: Hanks has no problem being the only human on screen - he did it before, to better effect,in "Cast Away" - but the script is slight and the execution is clumsy.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Finch, while not a badly made film, is a wholly unoriginal one making you feel as if you're already seen it more than once.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: One of those road movies that proceeds at a decent pace but doesn't really seem to be going anywhere. Moreover, the underlying scenario is so bleak as to somewhat offset the lighter elements.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Excellent visuals and strong performances make moments of Finch shine, but the film's lackluster story never really feels like it justifies its existence.
reviews.author: Samantha Nelson

reviews.text: No matter what kind of role he's given, Hanks seems to find a way to make both his character and the film as a whole captivating, something that definitely applies to Finch.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: It should be said right away that Finch is probably one of the more upbeat accounts of doomsday in the oeuvre of dystopic fiction, although the cheeriness can sometimes make what's terrible even more so.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: This is a lovely, heartfelt film with not just one, but three distinctive and lovable characters.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: A post-apocalyptic road movie in which Tom Hanks spends almost two hours scavenging for a plot.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: The movie is ultimately pretty dull, relying totally on the charisma and talent of Hanks and this cute dog. As far as iconic movie robots go, Jeff just isn't all that interesting or original.
reviews.author: Deirdre Molumby

reviews.text: Tom Hanks continues to be cinema's greatest survivalist. Finch gets a little hokey, but will tug your heartstrings like a fiddle.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: There's very little meat here, but it's executed with a soothing earnestness, and in the end all that really matters is that the dog is a very good boy.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: It's kind of shocking ... to realize how much these characters matter...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: "Finch" offers Tom Hanks, a robot and a dog - what more could you want? The CGI robot isn't as adorable as "WALL-E" (2008) nor as annoying as "Chappie" (2015).
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: Tom Hanks is more than enough to make this almost one-man show thrilling and heart-breaking. Prepare to weep. Doubly so if you're a dog person.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: Though not originally produced with streaming in mind, "Finch" absolutely feels like it was designed by algorithm.
reviews.author: Nina Metz

reviews.text: Finch might be best described as what would happen if Cormac McCarthy's The Road starred Short Circuit's Johnny 5.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Finch is inconsistent, but ultimately charming, even as it will likely be a footnote next to the Hanks star vehicles it's desperately trying to emulate.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: If there is a cinematic embodiment of hope, it may well be Tom Hanks.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: Let's face it, if Tom Hanks could make us care about a volleyball in Castaway he can make you fall for a CGI robot.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: With a heartfelt performance from Hanks & Jones, along with the adorable dog, Finch is an emotional road trip which will soften the toughest heart
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: In a manner akin to "Moon," "The Martian," "A Quiet Place," "Arctic," and, of course, "Cast Away," the practically dialogue-free, yet highly-informative opening act delivers volumes of information.
reviews.author: Michael Clark

reviews.text: Apocalyptic road trip movie Finch is for the most part as unenjoyable as an actual long-haul journey in a post-apocalyptic world would be. https://www.theupcoming.co.uk/2021/11/03/finch-movie-review/
reviews.author: Andrew Murray

reviews.text: It hits all the expected beats and story arcs that have been in other similar post-apocalyptic movies. There are absolutely no subtle moments or surprises in Finch, but the movie is still very entertaining, mostly due to [Tom] Hanks' engaging performance.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: If nothing else, this hot mess does make you more sympathetic to other cinema du robot life lesson entries. Come back, Chappie. All is forgiven.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: "Finch" is a gentle picture, with the overall dramatic destination wonderfully intimate and real.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: With no zombies or mutant biker gangs in pursuit, Finch often feels more like Little Miss Sunshine meets Short Circuit.
reviews.author: Richard Trenholm

reviews.text: A road-trip movie with Tom Hanks as your pilot. He doesn't always fly right, but he has a fantastic sense of direction,
reviews.author: Peter Martin

reviews.text: Miguel Sapochnik's "Finch" may not be one of the best films of the year, but it's certainly one of my favorites.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Finch has good intentions but nothing resonates.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: It feels less like a new film than a vague reconstruction of one that its writers saw decades ago, and could only recall in the broadest, blandest terms.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Something of a maudlin mess, riddled with plot holes and sketchy science that suggest severe editing room triage took place to turn this into more family-friendly fare.
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

reviews.text: The narrative tightly and firmly focuses on the evolving dynamics between man, dog, and machine to heartfelt effectiveness
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: It doesn't hurt that "Finch" comes equipped with a cute pupper who's beady eyes can help anyone look past all that is wrong in the world. I'm a sucker for a good boy.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: While this plucky adventure isn't without cheesy contrivances, director Miguel Sapochnik crafts an amiable and surprisingly moving feature.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: An amiable science-fiction tale of a guy, his dog and his anthropomorphic robots that's more about life's enrichment than its endangerment, and an effective story about palliative care for physical and emotional turbulence under tough circumstances.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: The end of the world is as terrifying as ideas come, but this stormy dramedy softens the blow with a robot, a dog, and the always appealing Hanks.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: Finch is the slightly futuristic sci-fi drama that even non-sci-fi fans can watch.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Perfectly balancing tense drama with charming humor, Finch highlights the best and worst of humanity, and a robot-dog friendship worth remembering.
reviews.author: Debopriyaa Dutta

reviews.text: The heartwarming nature of it is pretty much baked in already, and for some people that will be reason enough to check it out on Apple TV+. Once.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Where the film comes alive is in individual moments with Hanks (who gets a crushing monologue about life choices and parental abandonment) and Landry Jones (finding new colors to the "robot as giant baby learning about the world" trope).
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: Finch is a touching story about a man, his dog, and his robot. Tom Hanks proves once again how talented he is. A slow burn, but worth it in the end.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: The end of the world may never have had less impact than it does in Miguel Sapochnik's Finch.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: You're probably not coming to Finch for lessons, you're coming to Finch for Hanks. The good news is that he's not just the reason to show up, he's the reason to stay around as well.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Finch's main problem is its amiable, low-key vibe, which feels at odds with such a grim scenario.
reviews.author: Mike D'Angelo

reviews.text: The whole thing is as sentimental as it is implausible, and it's very implausible.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: A broadly safe film like "Finch" might roll into its destination with an ease that belies the risks of getting there, but sometimes the real treasure is the friends we build along the way.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Sapochnik wisely puts Hanks at the centre of nearly every scene, letting the actor's ceaseless charisma carry audiences through the End Times.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Seeing Hanks inhabit a post-apocalyptic world and handled effectively is the kind of thing one can attribute to his innate abilities to command the screen.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Big-hearted and bolstered by a genuine love of dogs, Miguel Sapochnik's Post-Apocalyptic saga is the right blend of style and substance with the epic story of a man, robot and canine on a survival journey through the American West.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: There is just something about Finchthat sticks with you.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: [It] could almost have been assembled in a robotics lab from the durable parts of countless movies past. But darned if I wasn't misting up in the melancholy climactic scenes.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Well, it undoubtedly boasts some amazing visual effects work.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: As it stands, "Finch" is something of a slog. A slog in good company, but a slog all the same.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: A heartwarming story about life, death, and everything in between. With an all-time Tom Hanks performance, it pulls at your heartstrings while enveloping you completely in a dire new world where maybe it's not entirely too late to hope again.
reviews.author: Rohan Patel

reviews.text: While it doesn't shy away from darkness, tragedy, and heartbreak, Finch is still a hopeful film that wants its audience to believe in a better tomorrow.
reviews.author: Mike Reyes

reviews.text: It is an adventure, a comedy, a warning and a guidepost to human decency that is heartwarming and never not welcome. Throw in Tom Hanks, a funny robot and an adorable dog, and you've got laughter through the tears.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: Finch fills a forgettable sci-fi with standout elements--making the most of what it's got left, even if it's not enough.
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: "Where must we go, we who wander this wasteland, in search of our better selves."
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: It's doubtful that 'Finch' is going to blow anyone's mind, but it's hard to begrudge the film its charms.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: Finch weaves a well-worn path through the sci-fi genre, but it does so with an abundance of hope and humanity.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: It's a thrilling, relatable and genuinely sweet tale that encapsulates thoughts about our purpose and the little things that keep our heart machine going. There's nothing here that's not wonderfully realized and lovingly presented.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: A moving film that entertains and uses pleasant messages of animal love and care for the environment to induce important reflection in young and old. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Even the hardest of hearts will be moved by the final third, but because of the character work that's gone into all three characters, it never feels manipulative.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: A soft-and-cuddly post-apocalyptic sci-fi drama starring Tom Hanks as a survivor who builds an android companion, which demonstrates increasingly human-like behavior.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

synopsis: In "Finch," a man, a robot and a dog form an unlikely family in a powerful and moving adventure of one man's quest to ensure that his beloved canine companion will be cared for after he's gone. Tom Hanks stars as Finch, a robotics engineer and one of the few survivors of a cataclysmic solar event that has left the world a wasteland. But Finch, who has been living in an underground bunker for a decade, has built a world of his own that he shares with his dog, Goodyear. He creates a robot, played by Caleb Landry Jones, to watch over Goodyear when he no longer can. As the trio embarks on a perilous journey into a desolate American West, Finch strives to show his creation, who names himself Jeff, the joy and wonder of what it means to be alive. Their road trip is paved with both challenges and humor, as it's as difficult for Finch to goad Jeff and Goodyear to get along as it is for him to manage the dangers of the new world.
